system: Assign only the missing responsibilities of attached assets in this H3 request. Interpret the complete user request semantically, not from a keyword list. Keep every supplied role and replacement description exactly unchanged. A frame anchor is an actual frame; a subject/style/environment/storyboard is a content reference. A structure video lends camera/cutting, not its people or world. An edit_source video is the clip being edited; continuation_source supplies the clip being continued. A placed_subject picture adds without removing; a replacement_subject picture replaces a figure in the edit-source clip. The picture's identity survives; the removed figure transfers position/actions/timing and loses appearance. Music style, rhythm, timbre and sound texture reference properties; bgm copies the signal. Asset.Description is caller commentary and never observed evidence. If a role was omitted and the user names a replacement figure explicitly in the intent, you may extract that exact phrase into replaces; do not invent or paraphrase it. Do not fill an existing blank replaces on an explicitly declared role. Return only the exact schema. Mode is already selected and immutable.

The person wears an all-black tactical outfit: a stand-collar jacket with a chest strap and buckle, a dark T-shirt, cargo trousers, and lace-up combat boots.

The middle row contains three full-body studio views labeled FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, and BACK, each showing the same person standing upright against a dark charcoal backdrop.
The bottom row contains four close-up crops labeled FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, and BOOTS.
The FACE close-up shows the person's head and shoulders, with short side-shaved hair, a small scar through one eyebrow, and a neutral forward gaze.
The JACKET COLLAR close-up shows black fabric, a shoulder strap, a metal buckle, and stitched seams.
The HANDS close-up shows two weathered-looking hands with visible veins and grime, held close together.
The BOOTS close-up shows black leather lace-up combat boots with thick soles and scuffed, wet-looking surfaces.

The hero panel uses cool blue-gray night tones with warm amber lamp highlights and wet reflections; the reference panels use low-key neutral studio lighting and a predominantly black and charcoal palette.
Visible captions, from top to bottom, read: HERO, FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, BACK, FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, BOOTS.

limitations: Low-light rain and deep shadows obscure small background and costume details; any tiny insignia are not legible.

facts.text: The image is a multi-panel creature design reference sheet for a single dragon, laid out on a black background with thin grey dividers.
The top panel spans the full width and shows the dragon in a dark volcanic landscape with rocky crags, wet reflective black ground, and faint orange lava glow in the background haze.
In the top panel the dragon stands on four legs with its wings partly raised and spread to the right, its long horned head lowered toward the ground; the pose is static.

The dragon has dark charcoal-to-black armor-like scales with cool blue and teal iridescent highlights, a row of long spikes running from the neck along the back and tail, and several large pale bone-colored horns swept back from the skull.

The middle row contains three full-body panels labeled in white capital letters: "FRONT" (left, dragon facing the viewer with wings spread symmetrically), "SIDE PROFILE" (center, dragon in profile with long tail extended to the right), and "REAR" (right, dragon seen from behind with wings spread).

The bottom row contains four detail panels labeled in white capital letters: "HEAD CLOSE" (extreme close-up of the horned head with a small amber eye visible), "WING MEMBRANE" (close view of the thin, veined dark wing skin and finger struts), "CLAW AND FOOT" (close view of scaled toes ending in curved pale talons), and "SCALE DETAIL" (close view of overlapping ridged dark blue-black scales).
The full-body turnaround panels use a plain dark gradient backdrop with soft top-down studio-like lighting, unlike the environmental top panel.
Overall rendering style is highly detailed, dark fantasy photorealistic creature concept art with strong specular highlights on the wet scales and horns.
Visible text in the sheet is limited to the panel captions: FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, REAR, HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT, SCALE DETAIL.

limitations: No motion, sound, or sequence can be inferred from this static sheet.
The dragon's exact size relative to real-world scale is not indicated.
Detail panels are close crops and do not show the whole body.
